newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST - Soft demand to dent Kohler yr shr.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Soft demand to dent Kohler yr shr.

text.p: A fall in consumer demand will dent South African paper and packaging company Kohler Ltd's year earnings growth, analysts said on Wednesday.
"Consumer demand has come off along with a slowdown in economic growth," said an analyst who asked not to be identified.

"The economy is the biggest single driving force behind the paper and packaging sector. Companies have not had a good time this year and they will have to come up with some new ideas to spur growth," the analyst said.
Kohler is due to announce results on Monday, October 22.
Analysts polled by Reuters forecast attributable earnings for the year to August 31 between 46 and 47.1 cents a share with a consensus 46.5 cents from 40.4 last year.
This translates into growth of 15 percent, well down on the 29 percent rate in the first six months.
They expected a dividend of 16 cents a share for the year.
Kohler's previous figures have been restated to take into account a 10-for-1 share split in February.
At the release of interim results in March, Kohler directors warned of a lower rate of growth in the second half amid a softening in consumer demand and an uncertain industry outlook.
